findings.title: TikZ graph shown as literal source
findings.evidence: The frozen body introduces the pictured two-component network, then places an unfenced center/tikzpicture environment at lines 49–62. The original-resolution tile visibly prints the TeX commands instead of showing two disconnected edges and their conductance/load labels. The diagram carries the network topology and values used by the example, so its loss is substantive to the visual explanation. Receipt reports tikz_count=0 and no diagram_failures; this is a renderer/path-handling gap, not a claim of malformed diagram mathematics.
findings.mapping: Two nodes (1,2) connected by c=1 and two nodes (3,4) connected by c=3; load labels b1=1, b2=b3=b4=0; no edge between components.
findings.source_line_map: The adjacent prose at lines 41–45 states disconnected components and incompatible component load; the caption at lines 47–48 identifies edges/conductances/masses/RHS; TikZ lines 50–61 encode two disjoint oriented edges and nodal RHS labels.

findings.title: TikZ network shown as literal source
findings.evidence: The original-resolution tile visibly exposes the unfenced TikZ source after the caption instead of rendering the three-compartment chain. Receipt reports tikz_count=0 and no diagram_failures. The diagram was intended to communicate graph orientation, conductances, masses, and node values; loss is a rendering defect, with no independent mathematical error alleged.
findings.mapping: Path 1→2→3, edge conductances c1=1 and c2=2, vertex masses m1=1,m2=2,m3=3.
findings.source_line_map: The caption at line 48 says orientation, conductances, and masses are displayed; the TikZ environment at lines 50–60 draws and labels the path.

findings.title: TikZ code block shown as literal source
findings.evidence: Tile --04 at original resolution shows the alleged drawing as lines of literal TikZ code at the end of the item, rather than a square split into two colored triangles with a shared diagonal. The fenced code block still fails to produce a diagram; receipt reports tikz_count=0 and no diagram_failures. The explanatory caption defines the two cells and their shared edge, so the rendered failure is concrete. No mathematical defect in the intended triangulation was found.
findings.mapping: Unit square with coordinate-order subdivision: blue K_(1,2)={0≤x2≤x1≤1}; orange K_(2,1)={0≤x1≤x2≤1}; shared red diagonal x1=x2; corner labels (0,0),(1,0),(0,1),(1,1).
findings.source_line_map: Remarks lines 158–162 explain the intended mapping; fenced `~~~tikz` begins at line 164 and closes at 178; line 179 ends the block.

findings.title: Consider a 2×2 checkerboard/null-mode sketch
findings.evidence: The counterexample is explicitly geometric: a four-cell 2×2 square mesh, alternating cellwise P0 values (+1 on the lower-left and upper-right cells, −1 on the other two), and the only interior Q1 node at the center. A compact labeled sketch would make the cancellation and the single-velocity-degree-of-freedom mechanism immediate. The prose and integrations are complete, so this is an editorial aid rather than a defect or a blocker.
findings.mapping: Four square cells; checkerboard signs + − / − + (lower-left and upper-right positive); one center Q1 hat, with zero boundary nodes. State that ∫q=0 and its coupling to the sole hat gradient is zero.
findings.source_line_map: Given geometry at line 43; checkerboard assignment and sole center node at line 51; gradient cancellation formulas at line 53; consequence for all velocities at line 55.
